clue.text: Limit cable production requiring two elements, maybe

indicators.note: a production is something made or worked up, so these letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets a ceiling on how much cable a factory turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' is the anagram signal: the ten letters of LIMIT CABLE rearranged. 'maybe' warns that the definition describes the answer by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bimetallic strip or coinage is made of two metals, and metals are chemical elements.

clue.text: Increase size of vessel to carry fifty

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so the vessel word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An instruction to enlarge a ship so it can take fifty passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloat is to swell, making something grow larger.

clue.text: Opaque material from which to drink pinta?

explanation.surface: A question about what substance one should sip a pint of milk from.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pinta' is British slang for a pint of milk, so the second reading is a glass for milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk glass is an opaque whitish glass; read literally it is a tumbler for drinking milk from.

clue.text: Delinquent twins burgle deli: one leaves here disgusted?

indicators.note: delinquent behaviour is wayward, so the letters that follow run wild into a new order
something that leaves departs, so the letter for one is dropped from the word deli

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Wayward twins rob a delicatessen and one of the customers walks out appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one leaves' removes I from DELI, leaving DEL; TWINS BURGLE DEL is then rearranged. 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells' is the stock pen name of an indignant letter-writer to British newspapers; the town is in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent spa town is proverbially home to the outraged letter-writer who signs off as Disgusted.

clue.text: Man was first to embrace polo playing

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside one's arms, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: someone who led was first, at the front

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the word polo frolicking out of order

explanation.surface: A man led the field in taking up the game of polo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the whole definition: a forename. 'playing' is the anagram signal and 'to embrace' the container signal; polo looks like the sport but only its letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, borne for example by kings of Belgium, serves as a male person in crosswords.

clue.text: Cool performance involving dancers?

parts.note: cool hints at frozen water rather than style, and the dancing performers glide on skates

explanation.surface: A trendy show with a troupe of dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged entertainment by skaters on a rink is a frozen spectacle featuring dancing.

clue.text: Extra cut in de luxe style

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: plush describes something luxurious and richly appointed

explanation.surface: A bonus trimmed in a luxurious manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or bonus on top of what is expected.

clue.text: Tormented soul grabbing one French king

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding inside
a tormented soul is twisted about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An anguished spirit seizes a monarch of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tormented' rearranges SOUL to LOUS, and 'grabbing' takes I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis was the name of many monarchs of France, such as the Sun King.

clue.text: It makes a change to mingle? Yes, apparently

indicators.note: making a change to letters means altering their order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says that getting out and socialising is a nice change, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes a change to' signals rearranging the letters of MINGLE and YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemingly and apparently both mean as far as one can tell.

clue.text: Tyre balance could show an arrangement in nature

parts.note: a radial is a type of car tyre
symmetry is balance between parts

explanation.surface: Garage talk: the way a tyre is balanced reveals a pattern found in nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Starfish and many flowers have body parts repeated around a central axis, a natural layout.

clue.text: Gold country, old, home of Disney World

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
land means a country

explanation.surface: A golden old country is where the theme park sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city is the site of Walt Disney World resort.

clue.text: Woman's hint to English person removed to safety

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name; the possessive adds no letters
a cue is a hint or prompt

explanation.surface: A lady gives an English person a tip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Evacuees, such as wartime children sent to the country, were moved away from danger.

clue.text: Hermit got upset by night flyer

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recluse was disturbed by something flitting about after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HERMIT GOT. The definition suggests a bat or owl, but it is the moth.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger moth is a striped moth that flies at night; it is also the name of a biplane.

clue.text: Japanese immigrant to US taken in by Miss Eisenhower

indicators.note: the letters are taken in, or held, by the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An incomer from Japan is welcomed by the President's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Issei is the term for a first-generation Japanese immigrant to America.

clue.text: Take care of a drug that's misused

indicators.note: misused letters are handled wrongly, so they are put in another order

explanation.surface: A warning to look after a drug that people abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard something is to protect or look after it.

clue.text: Mug up on an artist and writer, being a sticker?

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: the indefinite article gives A
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: Someone crams up on a painter and an author to be a stickler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MUG into GUM; 'Mug up' looks like the British phrase for swotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum arabic is an acacia resin used as an adhesive, so it makes things stick.

clue.text: Prosper, getting in good, round wood

parts.note: to do well is to prosper

explanation.surface: Thriving and getting in with the right people around the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowelling is cylindrical rod of timber, cut into pegs for joints.

clue.text: I'm to act as go-between next

parts.note: to mediate is to act between two parties

explanation.surface: A person announcing they will be the intermediary next.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means following straight after, with nothing in between.

clue.text: Explosion on motorway's a false news story

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece written on another follows it, so the explosion word comes after

parts.note: M is a motorway and 's stands for is
a report is a loud bang

explanation.surface: A blast on a motorway turns out to be a hoax news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosion' suggests a blast, but here it is the bang of a gun; 'on' places it after the motorway piece, whose 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misreport is an inaccurate account given in the press.

clue.text: See old boy act in menial capacity

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to serve is to work as a servant

explanation.surface: Watching a former pupil work as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to notice or watch.

clue.text: Only half of treads left — about a millimetre — that's a hindrance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pieces go round the others
only half of the word is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A tyre worn down to half its tread with only a millimetre left is a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half of' keeps the first three letters of treads; 'about' wraps those letters plus L around A and the millimetre symbol. The surface of a worn tyre is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trammel is something that restrains or impedes, originally a net or shackle.

clue.text: My, my, at last you could be highly desirable

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters might form something else when rearranged
at last picks only the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: An exclamation that you could, at last, be very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes U from YOU; MYMY plus U are rearranged by 'could be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummy means delicious, or by extension very attractive.

clue.text: Show clergyman at centre of duel

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

indicators.note: the centre of the word duel is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A vicar stands between two duellists.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical show of sketches and songs.

clue.text: She makes one cross

parts.note: cross suggests annoying someone, but it is the mark on a ballot paper

explanation.definitionFit: Someone casting a ballot in Britain marks an X beside a candidate.

clue.text: Resort thus housing government department, not on a regular basis

parts.note: a spa is a resort

indicators.note: housing means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
MoD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A resort accommodating a ministry, only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' is the container signal. The MoD is the British Ministry of Defence, and sic is the Latin word printed after a quotation to mean thus.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means occurring in fits and starts, intermittent.

clue.text: Swindle about eliminating race

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
a heat is a qualifying race that eliminates the slower runners

explanation.surface: A scam involving knocking out competitors in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat is to defraud.

clue.text: Drinks purveyor has nerve taking last of beer

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word beer

explanation.surface: A brewer has the gall to take the last of the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottler fills and sells drinks in bottles.

clue.text: The name, possibly, of a gas?

indicators.note: possibly indicates the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question about what a gas might be called.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Wire removed middle of apple, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to core an apple is to remove its centre

explanation.surface: A cable took out the centre of an apple, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is an electrical flex or thin rope.

clue.text: Get mad about badly managed poly's use of resources

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to dement is to drive mad

indicators.note: badly managed letters are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of poly; the possessive adds none

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry at how a polytechnic is badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly managed' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal. A poly was a British polytechnic college; dement is an old verb meaning to drive mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Deployment is the positioning of forces or assets for action.
